replacement: In these different governments all offices were at first elective. When the influence of wealth was out of the question, preference was given to merit, which gives a natural ascendancy, and to age, which is experienced in business and deliberate in council. The Elders of the Hebrews, the Gerontes at Sparta, the Senate at Rome, and the very etymology of our word Seigneur, show how old age was once held in veneration. But the more often the choice fell upon old men, the more often elections had to be repeated, and the more of a nuisance they became. Intrigues set in, factions were formed, party feeling grew bitter, and civil wars broke out. The lives of individuals were sacrificed to the pretended happiness of the State, and at length men were on the point of falling back into their primitive anarchy. Ambitious chiefs profited by these circumstances to make their offices permanent in their own families. At the same time the people, already used to dependence, ease and the conveniences of life, and already unable to break their fetters, agreed to an increase of their slavery in order to secure their tranquillity. Thus magistrates became hereditary. They grew used to considering their offices as a family estate, and themselves as proprietors of the communities of which they were at first only the officers. They regarded their fellow-citizens as their slaves and counted them, like cattle, among their belongings. They called themselves the equals of the gods and the kings of kings.
